The repair route is measurably hard, and both measurements were made rather than assumed: chair touching a thigh is inside the protection band by definition, so a connectivity-based separation has nothing to cut; and no threshold divides them, because the chair's mid-tones run 96 to 150 while the figure's own sub-knee edge pixels run 64 to 240. Raising the body-tone floor to 160 was tried, rendered and reverted — it takes the feet entirely and shreds the older woman's shins. Drive was not searched: the wave-a source sheets are in no cloud checkout, so a higher-resolution re-derivation cannot be attempted from here either.

generationRecipe: What is wanted is a seated adult body with NO furniture attached to it — no seat under the thighs, no chair leg against the shins. The scene supplies its own chair.

Either route satisfies this. ROUTE A, generate: draw a new seated figure, from the front, with no chair in the frame at all. ROUTE B, repair: take the four existing plates and remove the chair pixels that touch the figure, restoring the leg and foot contour underneath rather than cutting around it.

On route B specifically, an earlier automatic attempt removed about a pixel of the figure's own outline and the whole foot outline. That is what a threshold does to a contour and what a hand does not.
Either way: 8-bit RGBA, transparent where furniture would have been, at a width no smaller than the plates it replaces.
acceptanceCriteria: Shows a seated posture. The posture reads through bent-knees, horizontal-thighs, shins-vertical-to-floor, soles-flat-on-the-floor, seat-plane-between-the-thighs-where-the-chair-was. A figure that merely stands, or an upright figure with shorter legs, is wrong even when its contact points land correctly.
The figure faces front.

The posture is already drawn and is NOT being changed; these cues describe the four plates as they stand, so a redraw in a different posture would not satisfy this. What is asked for is the removal of chair pixels where they touch the figure, with the leg and foot contour restored underneath.
No furniture pixel anywhere against the legs, between the thighs, or beside the shins. The figure must be able to sit on a chair the room draws.
The leg and foot outline is continuous and unbroken. A plate that has lost its foot outline, or a pixel of its own contour, is a failed delivery even if every chair pixel is gone.
At least 669 pixels wide — the narrowest of the four plates this would replace — with real per-pixel transparency.
A genuinely seated posture: bent knees, horizontal thighs, shins vertical, soles on the floor. A standing figure with shortened legs is wrong even when its contact points land correctly.
